notes: Global South is a PRIORITY, not a filter: every country stays in the ranking.
opportunity = SI + income_bonus + novelty_bonus. SI (pure physical similarity) is always reported unchanged next to it.
Bonuses are additive points on the 0-100 SI scale, so a priority site can only overtake a site whose SI is at most `bonus` points higher. A clearly better analog in a high-income country still wins.
Bonuses apply only to candidates with SI >= min_si_for_bonus, so a weak analog is never promoted just because of where it is.
Income groups: World Bank classification (LIC/LMC/UMC/HIC), fetched by `python -m analog_atlas.cli fetch-income`.

novelty.notes: Wired (2026-11-14): novelty = clip(distance to the nearest analog field campaign in data/campaigns.csv / full_novelty_km, 0, 1). known_nearby flags candidates within known_nearby_km of a campaign or a catalog site (flag only, never removed).

access.notes: Travel time to the nearest city (Oxford MAP 2015, Earth Engine band raw_access_minutes). Linear: full bonus at <= 2 h, 0 at >= 24 h. > 48 h is flagged 'hard access', never removed.

cluster.notes: Greedy non-maximum suppression in opportunity order: one discovery per 150 km region.

selection.notes: HANDOFF 6.1. 'bonus': discoveries ordered by opportunity only. 'quota': the first top_n discoveries contain at least min_global_south Global South regions (best opportunity first, SI >= min_si_for_bonus); the remaining slots go to the best pure SI. Default 'quota' is a stated assumption pending the team's decision.
